parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is dominated by the national layer: a universal document regime forcing birth-sex markers on new passports, entry-screening instructions to refuse cases with document/sex discrepancy and to consider permanent fraud bars, documented confiscations stranding travellers, foreign-government advisories issued after detentions of foreign trans citizens, and documented custody harms (denial of hormones, forced labour, sexual abuse in immigration detention). These are traveller-facing universal-exposure measures with a state-threat-framing overlay, partially but incompletely checked by courts. The state layer is materially milder: no adult facility ban, no adult care ban, no sodomy law, marker changes available, but no gender-identity nondiscrimination or hate-crime coverage outside four municipalities. Severity: harassment, denial, refusal, and severe-but-rare custody abuse; imprisonment not typical. This sits near the 0.45 universal-exposure tier, lifted slightly by a non-hostile subnational layer and partial judicial pushback, and held down by documented detention abuse and fraud-bar exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: Universal: passports reissued as birth sex, X markers stopped; entry officers instructed to refuse on document/sex discrepancy and consider lifetime fraud ineligibility; confiscations reported stranding travellers; allied governments issue advisories after detentions.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; litigation ongoing; fraud finding requires four elements, waiver possible, 'never automatic'.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at entry can escalate to secondary inspection, refusal, or fraud allegation — the primary exposure chain.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented custody harms nationally: national prison policies forcing haircut removal of hormones and psychiatric 'correction'; immigration detention forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse; a trans visitor abroad can enter this system via any incident.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Several orders enjoined; courts have blocked some measures; not every traveller is detained.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry discrepancy → detention → birth-sex or hostile placement is a live, documented pathway.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal facility exclusion from congruent single-sex spaces; 4 states criminalise certain restroom use; in this state no adult facility ban — one school district restricts student bathrooms; federal order bars funded facilities.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State has no statewide adult facility ban; 29+ states and the capital district have no mapped ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor's exposure flips across state lines; federal facilities and schools restricted everywhere federally funded.

care_services.exposure: Medication continuity uncertain; national subpoenas of hospital records of minors; 27 states ban youth care; national insurance rule proposed; state medical board draft would make youth-care provision unprofessional conduct.
care_services.protection: No statewide adult-care ban in this state; several national orders enjoined; adult care formally lawful here.
care_services.interaction: An adult seeking refills is exposed to discretion; a travelling parent with a trans minor faces record-scrutiny and care-denial risk.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State threat-framing documented: 'radical gender ideology' framed alongside violent extremism; counterterrorism strategy targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups; bathroom arrest (trespass, men's ward holding) in one state.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Guidance states counterterrorism powers not aimed at mere disagreement; hate-crime statute covers gender identity nationally.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Framing licenses local enforcement discretion; enforcement intensity varies by state and locality.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling with a trans minor: care banned in 27 states; state board draft would discipline providers; teachers criminally prosecutable for facilitating social transition under an executive order; hospital records subpoenaed; school sports restricted here.
minors_guardians.protection: Draft regulation not yet operative (pending law-department review and comment); several orders enjoined; this state has no youth-care ban in force.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor's presence converts ordinary school, care or sports interactions into investigation or disclosure risks.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence count or homicide baseline for the state; bias-motivated violence lacks state penalty enhancement here; discrimination outside four municipalities has no recourse for a visitor.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute; four municipalities (~46% of population) prohibit gender-identity discrimination in public accommodations; police response otherwise not documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: An incident outside municipal coverage leaves the visitor with thin or no state-level remedy.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Open questions: which documents are believed at entry, facility placement if detained, medical-board final text, enforcement of municipal ordinances, actual violence rates — unresolved, and the national map is shifting between travel dates.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active litigation, a legal-aid FAQ, functioning courts that have enjoined several orders, and four municipal ordinances give partial, real but uneven remedies.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies work best against federal overreach slowly; against local discrimination they may not exist at all.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like 0.45-D, universal document/database exposure reaches every visitor regardless of discretion, with state operations sharing data and thin remedies. Here the exposure is even sharper at the border (refusal instructions, lifetime fraud bar), but no local registration regime; net roughly comparable, slightly above on some axes, slightly below on severity of fraud consequences.

0.55-C's ward assignment and partial care denial resemble the facility and care exposures here, but this jurisdiction adds national-level custody abuses and threat framing that 0.55-C lacks, pulling below that anchor; conversely its subnational layer is more protective than 0.55-C's rural improvisation.

0.75-C has trained, accountable border officers and functioning appeals with only brief detention. Here border treatment is openly hostile by instruction (refusals, fraud bars, confiscations, foreign advisories), and no comparable border remedy operates; the state layer alone would resemble 0.75-C, but the combined regime cannot reach that tier.

0.25-C features birth-sex custody placement with frequent assault and a criminal cross-dressing statute. This jurisdiction documents custody abuse but only for the detained minority, has no cross-dressing crime, no adult facility ban, and courts that partially restrain the state — materially above 0.25-C.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller's operative regime is the national document-and-entry system plus a mild-to-moderate state. The national layer imposes universal exposure — every passport check reveals or risks revealing status, and entry officers are instructed to refuse or investigate discrepancies, with a lifetime fraud bar available — and documented custody abuse raises the worst case well above administrative friction. Courts have enjoined parts of the regime and a hate-crime statute exists, but no documented remedy reliably reverses a border refusal or protects a detainee. The state adds no adult facility or care ban and offers marriage recognition and marker changes, but outside four municipalities a visitor has no anti-discrimination recourse and no bias-crime enhancement. With a trans minor, care-ban climate and record subpoenas add a distinct family-exposure layer. Net: friction, denial and humiliation are likely; severe custody outcomes possible but conditional; imprisonment for being trans is not the documented default.
